# Netsertive launches AI-native MLX 3.0 platform for multi-location marketing command centres

● 13 days ago

Netsertive has launched version 3.0 of its Multi-Location Experience Platform, transforming it into an AI-native marketing command centre for franchise and multi-location brands. The Morrisville-based marketing technology provider announced the update on 3 August.
The platform consolidates fragmented local data into a single source, enabling marketers to track performance and manage campaigns across multiple locations. It integrates AI models from Amazon Bedrock, Snowflake's Cortex, and Google's Gemini to deliver automated insights and recommendations.
Key features include an AI chat assistant, call insights tool, and a web content editor for managing distributed location pages.
The platform also offers an interactive directory showing which marketing products and services individual locations have activated.
Netsertive serves over 1,500 retailers, franchises, and auto dealers.

_**The next-generation platform turns fragmented local data into an interactive, proactive Marketing Command Center for franchise and multi-location brands.**_

**MORRISVILLE, NC / [ACCESS Newswire](https://www.accessnewswire.com/) / August 3, 2026 /** Netsertive, a marketing technology platform provider for multi-location and franchise brands, today announced the official launch of the latest version of its innovative Multi-Location Experience (MLX) Platform.

Meanwhile, the new Active Location Directory and interactive map boost network visibility, instantly showing corporate teams the marketing products and services that locations have activated, editing location details, and refining lead routing rules.

# Yesterday’s Marketing Technology & AI News | August 3, 2026

By [Agile Brand Guide](https://agilebrandguide.com/author/agilebrandguide/) Aug 4, 2026 [News](https://agilebrandguide.com/category/news/) [Yesterday's News](https://agilebrandguide.com/category/news/yesterdays-news/)

11 Minute Read 0

Yesterday’s press releases paint a picture that is simultaneously exciting and sobering for [Chief Marketing Officers (CMOs)](https://agilebrandguide.com/wiki/roles-teams/chief-marketing-officer/) . The dominant theme is not that AI is arriving — it is already here, operating in production, and beginning to expose the gaps between what marketing organizations thought they were building and what they actually need.
The announcements from August 3, 2026 reveal three uncomfortable truths that CMOs should sit with before celebrating vendor milestones.

**The personalization paradox is getting worse, not better.** [Optimizely’s](https://list.agilebrandguide.com/companies/optimizely-inc) research showing that 75% of UK consumers regularly receive irrelevant marketing is a damning indictment of the current AI-in-marketing moment. Vendors have been promising hyper-personalization for years, and AI tools have proliferated across marketing stacks — yet the consumer experience is deteriorating. The problem is not a lack of AI tools; it is that AI has been deployed primarily to accelerate content production, not to improve relevance. Marketing teams are generating more content faster, but without the data infrastructure, audience intelligence, or workflow discipline to make that content land. CMOs need to ask a hard question: are we using AI to do more of the wrong things at scale?
**Agentic commerce is not a 2027 problem — it is a 2026 operational reality.** The WooCommerce/IDC research projecting $500 billion in AI-replatformed digital spending by 2030 sounds like a future-state forecast, but the underlying finding is immediate: AI agents are already shopping on behalf of buyers, and 40% of agentic automation will enhance enterprise applications by 2027. For CMOs, this means the discovery funnel is being restructured right now. AI agents do not respond to brand storytelling, emotional creative, or even SEO-optimized content in the traditional sense — they evaluate structured data, verified inventory, and pricing accuracy. Marketing teams that have not audited their product data quality and structured content infrastructure are already losing ground in agent-mediated discovery, even if their dashboards do not show it yet.

**The attribution gap is widening as fast as new ad channels emerge.** [CTM’s](https://list.agilebrandguide.

...

The question for CMOs is not whether to adopt agentic AI, but which workflows to automate first, what human oversight looks like at scale, and how to measure the quality of AI-conducted interactions against human benchmarks. These are not technology decisions; they are organizational design decisions that most marketing teams are not yet equipped to make.

Meanwhile, Netsertive’s MLX 3.0 launch and NIQ’s IFA 2026 positioning both reflect a maturing market dynamic: the platforms that will win are those that consolidate fragmented data into actionable intelligence, not those that add more features to already-complex stacks. For multi-location and franchise brands, the promise of a single AI-native command center is compelling — but the implementation reality requires clean data, consistent taxonomy, and organizational alignment that most brands have not yet achieved.
NIQ’s framing of AI-driven decision-making at IFA is similarly aspirational; the gap between having AI-powered insights and having the organizational capability to act on them in real time remains significant.

The strategic decisions CMOs need to make this week are concrete: audit your product data quality for agent-mediated discovery readiness; evaluate whether your AI content investments are improving relevance or just volume; ensure your marketing operations team has a channel evaluation process that precedes budget allocation; and identify one or two high-volume, repetitive workflows where agentic AI can deliver measurable productivity gains without sacrificing quality oversight. The vendors will keep announcing. The CMOs who win will be the ones who have a framework for deciding what actually matters.

* * *

## **Here’s The News:**

**Netsertive Announces the Latest AI-Native Version of MLX, Introduces Version 3.
0 of its Multi-Location Experience Platform** — Netsertive, a marketing technology platform provider for multi-location and franchise brands, officially launched MLX Platform 3.0, repositioning the product from a data analytics and campaign management tool into what the company calls a proactive Marketing Command Center. The new version layers an AI-native engine over a consolidated localized data infrastructure, enabling multi-location marketers to eliminate data silos, query performance data conversationally, and execute campaigns across hundreds of locations simultaneously. Key new capabilities include an MLX Chat Assistant, AEO for AI-search optimization, and Call Insights AI. The platform integrates best-of-breed AI models including Amazon Bedrock/Nova Micro, Snowflake Cortex, and Google Gemini, selecting the appropriate model for each task. The company says the platform shifts the paradigm from displaying lagging data to delivering actionable, narrative-driven recommendations.
[Read the full press release](https://www.pressrelease.com/news/netsertive-announces-the-latest-ai-native-version-of-mlx-introduces-version-3-0) .

**Three-Quarters of Consumers Say the Marketing They Receive Is Irrelevant — Optimizely Research** — Optimizely released new UK consumer research on August 3, 2026, revealing that 75% of UK consumers regularly receive marketing that is irrelevant to them. The survey of 1,000 UK consumers and 100 UK marketers found that 69% of consumers often receive duplicate messages or emails from brands, 61% feel overwhelmed by the volume of marketing they receive, and 42% disengage when content feels irrelevant. On the marketer side, 60% say they often launch campaigns without the time or data needed to optimize them, 66% say managing multiple tools creates unnecessary work, and 54% move from campaign to campaign without properly evaluating performance.

# Netsertive’s MLX 3.0 Doesn’t Just Report Local Marketing. It Starts Running It.

August 3, 2026

By: [James Vance](https://newsroom.seaprwire.com/james-vance/) – [SeaPRwire](https://newsroom.seaprwire.com) – Multi-location marketers still live in a quiet panic. Data sits in one spreadsheet. Campaign results hide in another tool. Revenue impact never quite lines up. Franchise owners and corporate teams spend more time reconciling numbers than acting on them. Speed of change feels glacial. Visibility arrives late. That gap between knowing and doing has become the real bottleneck for local growth. Netsertive just put a name and a platform version number on the problem.

The company launched MLX Platform version 3.0 as an AI-native Marketing Command Center. It sits on top of a consolidated localized data infrastructure. The goal is straightforward. Eliminate the silos. Give multi-location marketers and individual location owners direct control of their digital presence.
Track full-funnel performance with accuracy. The platform pulls performance data into one source of truth. Users can query it without jumping between CRMs and isolated dashboards. They can measure true revenue impact. They can run campaigns that respond faster. AI sits at the core rather than as an add-on. Tools include the MLX Chat Assistant, AEO for AI-search, and Call Insights AI. These surface trends automatically. They flag optimization chances. They generate content. They deliver narrative recommendations straight to the user. Herb Brittner, VP of Product and Engineering, put it plainly. The shift moves from lagging data displays to clear, actionable insights that show exactly what drives local growth. The architecture leans on best-of-breed models and serverless functions. Amazon Bedrock with Nova Micro. Snowflake Cortex. Google Gemini.
Each model handles the job it fits best—predicting lead generation, running an AI chat agent on performance data, or optimizing digital channels across two hundred locations. Self-service controls sit beside the intelligence. The Web Content Editor lets marketers manage distributed location pages and push localized updates from one place. The Active Location Directory and interactive map give corporate teams instant sight of which marketing products and services each location has activated. They can edit location details and refine lead routing rules without extra layers of process. Netsertive positions the release as a new benchmark. Multi-location brands can now scale local growth beyond static reporting into proactive, AI-driven execution, visibility, and speed. More than 1,500 retailers, franchises, auto dealers, and media companies already use the company’s broader solutions.

# Netsertive Announces the Latest AI-Native Version of MLX, Introduces Version 3.0 of its Multi-Location Experience Platform

Press Release • Aug 3, 2026

_**The next-generation platform turns fragmented local data into an interactive, proactive Marketing Command Center for franchise and multi-location brands.**_

* 
* 
* 
* 

[](https://cdn.nwe.io/files/x/d8/72/d1f43eb7ed2f3644aeb9ebbac72e.png)

**MORRISVILLE, N.C., August 3, 2026 (Newswire.com) -** Netsertive, a marketing technology platform provider for multi-location and franchise brands, today announced the official launch of the latest version of its innovative Multi-Location Experience (MLX) Platform. The reimagined Platform transitions from traditional data analytics and campaign management into an actionable, proactive Marketing Command Center.

...

AI-powered tools, including MLX Chat Assistant, AEO for AI-search and Call Insights AI, automatically surface performance trends, identify optimization opportunities, generative content and deliver narrative recommendations directly to users.

"By embedding AI-native capabilities into the platform's core infrastructure, we are shifting the paradigm from displaying lagging data to providing clear, actionable insights that reveal exactly what is driving local growth," says Herb Brittner, VP of Product and Engineering at Netsertive.

"The latest version of the platform seamlessly leverages best-of-breed models and serverless AI functions such as Amazon's Bedrock/Nova Micro, Snowflake's Cortex and Google's Gemini, ensuring that the right model is being used for the right job-whether predicting lead generation, using an AI-chat agent to analyze performance, or optimize digital marketing channels across 200 locations."
To ensure these insights lead to immediate action, MLX pairs native intelligence with powerful self-service controls like the Web Content Editor-enabling marketers to effortlessly manage distributed location pages and make localized content updates centrally. Meanwhile, the new Active Location Directory and interactive map boost network visibility, instantly showing corporate teams the marketing products and services that locations have activated, editing location details, and refining lead routing rules.

With MLX 3.0, Netsertive has set a new benchmark for how multi-location brands can scale local growth, moving the industry fully beyond static reporting into an era of proactive, AI-driven execution, visibility and speed.

For more information or to schedule a Platform walkthrough, contact us at [www.netsertive.com](https://stats.nwe.io/x/html?
